findings.title: R27 drops the third mandatory birth duty for ordinary detectors
findings.body: R27 lets a new detector, gate, watcher, census, or detector-shaped test ship with a bite-proof, keep-or-retire entry, and reader. Spec A requires every detector to have a third birth duty: by-construction coverage. R27 mentions that duty only for hand-maintained parallel enumerations, so all seventeen children quote a weaker admission rule.
findings.suggestion: Add by-construction coverage to R27's requirements for every new detector-shaped component, retaining the parallel-enumeration clarification as an application of that general duty.
findings.evidence: Spec A FR-B2 says a detector is admitted only with all three duties, including scope complete by construction (specs/spec-a-doctrine.md:570-579). R27's general list omits coverage and applies it only to parallel enumerations (package/register.md:122); every child consumes R27 (package/register.md:124).

findings.title: The plugin-root seam and its lint disappear from the decommission scope
findings.body: The acceptance bullet allocated between C9 and C15 also says the plugin-root seam and its lint have met their delete-when condition. Neither R15 nor C15 names that pair, so the package provides no owner or DoD for retiring it.
findings.suggestion: Add the plugin-root seam and its lint to R15 and C15, state whether their retirement is unconditional or receipt-dependent as the spec implies, and add a corresponding DoD check.
findings.evidence: Spec A names the plugin-root seam and lint immediately before the harness_probe outcome (specs/spec-a-doctrine.md:809-814). Coverage assigns the entire FR-B6 bullet to C9/C15 (package/coverage-map.md:93), but R15 omits the seam (package/register.md:74) and C15 enumerates only the six pieces, heartbeat, harness_probe, re-arm request, and quota work (package/children/C15.md:3).

findings.title: C17 replaces FR-E1's four declared dependencies with a different set
findings.body: C17 says calibration checks a collector, a pinned registry surface, the kind labels, and a vet-receipt lane field. The stamped dependency list is instead: a launch ledger; a collector with pinned registry; a consumer path for keep-or-retire back-fill; and the detector-shaped-test boundary. Following this body would omit three required checks and split one dependency into two.
findings.suggestion: Replace the parenthetical dependency list with FR-E1's four actual dependencies and make the DoD name and exercise those four explicitly. Keep kind-label creation as its separate acceptance requirement.
findings.evidence: The authoritative list is enumerated in Spec A FR-E1 (specs/spec-a-doctrine.md:1006-1020). C17's substituted list appears in its What (package/children/C17.md:3), while its DoD refers only generically to 'the four declared dependencies' (package/children/C17.md:8).

findings.title: C1 does not carry the two FR-B5 criteria allocated to it
findings.body: The coverage map assigns FR-B5's tight-hard-shell emphasis and at-the-door defect-evidence rule to C1, but C1 only promises the earlier shrink-or-tolerate posture. Neither its What nor its DoD lands the rule that in-envelope variance is not defect evidence or the rule for bounded soft variance.
findings.suggestion: Either add both allocated FR-B5 rules to C1's PHILOSOPHY scope and DoD, or reassign them to the child and one-home surface that will actually land the front-door behavior.
findings.evidence: Spec A separately requires a tight hard shell and defines when variance is defect evidence (specs/spec-a-doctrine.md:775-782). Coverage assigns both bullets to C1 (package/coverage-map.md:90-91), while C1 names and grades only 'Change 5's posture' (package/children/C1.md:3,6).

findings.title: C13 owns all of FR-D9 but scopes itself only to the three-question note
findings.body: The map assigns all six FR-D9 acceptance bullets to C13, but C13's anchor and body cover only the three successor-design answers. No child or register entry lands the concrete three-condition tripwire, the pre-deletion coverage replay, the open-window sequencing rule, or the pinned prior-version back-out.
findings.suggestion: Expand C13's body and DoD to land and grade every FR-D9 rule in the appropriate reference, or split those bullets explicitly to another child with an exact boundary.
findings.evidence: Coverage assigns FR-D9 bullets 1-6 to C13 (package/coverage-map.md:219-224). C13 limits FR-D9 to 'the three answers' and grades only the design note (package/children/C13.md:1,3,10). The omitted rules are normative acceptance criteria in Spec B (specs/spec-b-re-derivation.md:865-894).

findings.title: C7 omits several requirements inside the charter document-layer criterion
findings.body: C7 carries the map shape and one-hop references, but omits the same acceptance bullet's hierarchy-by-branch, conditional pointer wording, leading-words rule, no-op test, stable-first cache rule, and prohibition on duplicating script-enforced rules as prose. Its DoD therefore permits a charter rewrite that satisfies only part of the allocated criterion.
findings.suggestion: Add the omitted document-layer rules to C7's What and grade them in the DoD, preferably by mapping each rule to the affected charter sections in the PR body.
findings.evidence: The complete document-layer acceptance bullet contains these requirements (specs/spec-a-doctrine.md:825-835) and is wholly assigned to C7 (package/coverage-map.md:96). C7's What and DoD mention only duty sections, completion criteria, links, and excuse tables (package/children/C7.md:3,6-8).

findings.title: The conformance-probe DoD does not test the failed-probe launch decision
findings.body: The DoD checks only that a broken engine produces a loud failure naming the engine and failure. It does not demonstrate that nothing launches without the owner's word, that dependent lanes are named, or that a missing second family is substituted or parked. Those are the safety-relevant outcomes of the probe contract.
findings.suggestion: Add a recorded failed-probe wave covering both owner choices and assert that launch is blocked before the word; when proceeding, assert that dependent lanes and the substitute-family-or-park outcome are recorded.
findings.evidence: Spec B requires the preflight to name dependent lanes, place the launch-or-hold choice beside the launch word, prohibit launch without that word, and substitute or park affected full lanes (specs/spec-b-re-derivation.md:1079-1091). C11's DoD verifies only the loud diagnostic (package/children/C11.md:10).

findings.title: C11 never grades secret scrubbing on the new native channels
findings.body: C11 verifies typed results, schema validation, and removal of the marker parser, but no DoD bullet proves that secrets are scrubbed after codex—and conditionally cursor—move to native result channels. A PR could satisfy every listed check while bypassing a hard-shell boundary requirement.
findings.suggestion: Add planted-secret tests for each channel C11 moves, asserting the typed result and journal are scrubbed, alongside the malformed-result refusal tests.
findings.evidence: The native-channel ruling explicitly keeps secret scrubbing and fail-closed parsing on the new channel (specs/spec-b-re-derivation.md:954-957), and R9 repeats that requirement for every channel (package/register.md:50). C11's DoD covers schema validity and malformed results but not scrubbing (package/children/C11.md:6-11).

findings.title: C14 does not grade secret scrubbing or malformed-result refusal for Claude
findings.body: C14 adds two new Claude result paths but only verifies successful typed results, acknowledgement handling, configuration refusal, and telemetry. It has no DoD case showing that a malformed Claude result refuses or that secrets are scrubbed in print and background modes.
findings.suggestion: Add malformed-result and planted-secret cases for both Claude modes, asserting the common refusal shape and that neither the result nor journal exposes the secret.
findings.evidence: R9 requires secret scrubbing and refuse-on-malformed on every engine channel (package/register.md:50), and Spec B applies the same discipline to each supported mode (specs/spec-b-re-derivation.md:1095-1109). C14's DoD has no corresponding checks (package/children/C14.md:6-10).

findings.title: Dropped MOVE rows are not required to prove that they echo nothing
findings.body: The corrected contract requires dropped MOVE rows to read nothing, resolve no caller input, and echo nothing. C10's DoD checks only that they read nothing, leaving the newly clarified no-echo behavior ungraded.
findings.suggestion: Amend the row-level DoD to require a recorded dropped-input case with no resolved-input or echo field, and reconcile that assertion against the dated annex closing note.
findings.evidence: R8 states all three properties (package/register.md:46), while C10's DoD states only that a dropped row 'reads nothing' (package/children/C10.md:7).

findings.title: C15's repository-wide quota grep cannot pass against the committed package
findings.body: The DoD says a grep for quota in the plugin may return only the parked module and glossary history note, but the decomposition artifacts are committed and C15, R14, and R15 themselves contain quota text. The criterion is mechanically unsatisfiable as written.
findings.suggestion: Scope the grep to the runtime and doctrine surfaces whose quota leg is being retired, explicitly excluding the committed decomposition/history artifacts, and name the exact allowed residual paths.
findings.evidence: The package README says these decomposition artifacts are committed (package/README.md:11-18). The asserted repository-wide grep is at package/children/C15.md:8, while quota remains intentionally present in C15's own body and quoted register entries (package/children/C15.md:3,16,18).
